issues.description: Test changes add a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash addition that likely fails MAX_COIN_AMOUNT/__post_init__ or burns funds silently
issues.detail: Tests now pass additions=[Addition(amount=0, puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)]. The original calls used empty additions to exercise the legacy amount/inner_address path. Replacing with a zero-amount/zero-hash addition either changes the assertion (now exercises additions path) or creates a coin sent to puzzle_hash zero, masking the prior coverage rather than testing the refactor's backward compatibility.

issues.description: send_transaction now rejects non-XCH addresses but previously only checked prefix; behavior regression for callers
issues.detail: Original code compared only the configured network prefix. New code calls ensure_valid_address with allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}, which will reject TXCH on testnets or any other valid prefix the old logic accepted. This silently narrows accepted inputs and can break existing clients/tests on non-mainnet networks.

issues.description: cat_spend address validation forces XCH allowed_types but inner_address for CATs is typically a non-CAT inner puzzle hash; may still be misnamed
issues.detail: When request.additions is None, inner_address is decoded through ensure_valid_address with allowed_types={AddressType.XCH}. CAT inner addresses historically may have been encoded with txch/xch prefixes, but downstream behavior previously accepted whatever decode_puzzle_hash produced. Restricting types could break clients that previously sent CAT-prefixed addresses.

issues.description: send_transaction loses per-address MAX_COIN_AMOUNT check and memo encoding semantics
issues.detail: Old code encoded memos as bytes via mem.encode('utf-8') before passing to generate_signed_transaction. New path passes request.memos (list[str]) into Addition.memos directly. If create_signed_transaction's downstream pipeline still expects pre-encoded bytes for memos, encoding behavior differs. Worth verifying Addition.memos handling preserves identical wire format.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation uses `None in {set}` which de-duplicates and may also conflict with unhashable values
issues.detail: Using a set literal `None in {extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution}` requires all elements be hashable. tail_reveal/tail_solution are bytes (hashable, fine), but the pattern is fragile and duplicates the same check already done in the first branch. Prefer `any(x is None for x in ...)` for clarity and to mirror the explicit None checks above.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction now silently accepts CAT-only fields without wallet-type validation
issues.detail: extra_delta/tail_reveal/tail_solution/puzzle_decorator added to CreateSignedTransaction with no guard that the target wallet is a CATWallet. A caller hitting create_signed_transaction directly on a standard Wallet with these set will have cat_discrepancy propagated and likely fail deep in generate_signed_transaction. Validating wallet type vs. CAT fields at request boundary would surface errors earlier.

review.summary:
The refactor centralizes transaction creation but introduces several backward-compatibility risks: send_transaction's address validation is narrowed to XCH-only (rejecting valid testnet prefixes previously accepted by prefix-only checks), and cat_spend's inner_address path is similarly constrained. Test changes substitute non-empty additions for empty ones in ways that may either fail validation or alter what the tests actually cover. CreateSignedTransaction now accepts CAT-specific fields without wallet-type guards, and minor cleanups to the extracted cat_discrepancy_validation helper would improve clarity.</summary>
